mechanism: exec-WM's GATE B (detect_translation: a move must explain EVERY interior diff cell, `if diffset - departures - arrivals: continue`) was measured on 2026-08-27 to discard 641 of 2394 move-action transitions (26.8%), the largest single loss channel, and was ranked far above GATE A on that raw size. Sub-classifying those 641 by the geometry of the leftover cells -- is the leftover itself one translation (co-mover), small and spatially disjoint from the sprite (bystander), touching the sprite footprint (overlap), or large/many-component (diffuse) -- separates the part a repair could actually recover from the part it could not.
summary: 641 residual transitions reproduce exactly. Split: overlap 354 (55.2%, median leftover 35 cells), co-mover 126 (19.7%, median 4), bystander 117 (18.3%, median 2), diffuse 44 (6.9%). Recoverable = co-mover + bystander = 243 of 641 (37.9%), i.e. at most 10.3% of all 2394 transitions rather than the advertised 26.8%. Sensitivity sweep of the one free parameter (bystander cell bound) over 2..20 leaves co-mover fixed at 126 and overlap fixed at 354 by construction, and moves recoverable only within 197-246 (30.7-38.4%).
lesson: The size of a loss channel is not the size of the win available from repairing it: GATE B's headline 641 is 2.6x its own recoverable subset, and its majority class (overlap, 55%) is untouched by either repair that was proposed for it -- a bounded-leftover tolerance would actively mis-mine there. This REVERSES the previous day's ranking of GATE B over GATE A on the strength of the previous day's own named follow-up. Measure what a fix would recover, not what the bug discards, before ranking fixes. Two failed drafts also re-confirm that an instrument must reuse the shipped primitives AND their initialisation: a fresh, unconverged HudMask silently reclassifies every transition, and detect_translation never emits the label the tracer does.
